author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-16 on memway's own map: UNIQUENESS IS BEING TREATED AS CERTAINTY, and it hands ~23% of call edges to the wrong target at high confidence.

`conf, how = 0.95, "exact"` is set the moment ix.resolve() returns anything, before anything checks HOW it resolved. resolve() falls back to bare-name matching, so a short name with exactly ONE definition anywhere in the repo becomes the target for every call of that name - including calls the repo never defines, i.e. stdlib and builtin methods.

Measured: 369 of 1627 call edges (23%) land on an entity whose short name is a stdlib/builtin method. Two of them absorb 295 edges between them - 18% of every call edge in the map:

  tests.test_console.get                                     159 incoming
  tests.test_version...test_editable_marker...D.read_text    136 incoming

The second is a one-line stub class D defined INSIDE a test function. Every `p.read_text()` in the package - access_cache.load_json_cached, cli._is_editable, cli.plan_rules_write - is attributed to it, at confidence 0.95, labelled "exact". `get` collects every `dict.get()` in the repo including from docs/examples.

Two consequences. Visually it is why the graph has a hairball: two meaningless nodes act as magnets for a fifth of all edges. Analytically it is worse - fan_in on those stubs is fiction, and the blast radius of anything that reaches them is inflated by hundreds of false paths.

The D11b tiebreak (prefer production over tests when a bare name is ambiguous) cannot help here: it only fires when there is competition, and these names have exactly one definition. No competition is being read as high confidence when it is the case that most deserves suspicion.

Wanted: a bare-name fallback must not score "exact". Either drop to the low-confidence tier (<0.7, which the grounding block already surfaces and warns about), or refuse to resolve a receiver-method call whose name is defined only inside a test scope or a function-local class. Do not special-case a list of stdlib names - the rule is about HOW it resolved, not about which names Python happens to ship.

author: cli
text: SUPERSEDES the DEFECT note below. Fixed in 0.54.3; that note is history - read it for the measurements, not for what this code does. What holds now: _unreachable_target rejects three things a bare name can never legally be. (1) FUNCTION-LOCAL targets: a class or def inside a function body cannot be named from outside it. (2) AN ATTRIBUTE CALL IS NOT A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION: d.get(x) cannot be 'def get' at module scope - RawEdge.via_attr carries the fact the parser used to discard, which is why PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION went 4 to 5. (3) PRODUCTION CODE DOES NOT CALL TEST HELPERS. All three are facts about scope, deliberately not a list of stdlib names - such a list is endless, language-specific, and wrong the moment a repo legitimately defines get. Result here: read_text 136->0 incoming, get 159->19, 850 edges dropped. THE THING THAT WILL BITE NEXT: FOUR tiers in this method match on a short name - exact, annotated, inherited-guess, bare-name fallback. The first pass guarded two and the others kept feeding the same false hubs until re-measuring found them; reading the code had not. test_units_core2 now walks build() by AST and fails if ANY comprehension touching _by_short lacks a guard. Do not move the guard into resolve(): rules 2 and 3 are about the caller, which resolve() has no business knowing.
